sources: TUESDAY Oct 6 2026 RUN (06:20 UTC, pre-US-open - market fields are Oct 5 US closes plus live Asian/European session where available). HEADLINE: THE CREDIT STREAK BROKE AND THE DOLLAR BROKE OUT. Two of the dashboard hard signals reversed direction in the same session: HY OAS tightened 14bp, ending a nine-session widening run, while DXY took out its 102.21 52-week high and the 10y closed at 5.315 pct, the highest since 2007. The squeeze is rotating out of credit and oil and into the dollar and the long end. CREDIT - THE STREAK IS OVER: HY OAS 310bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, 3.10 pct dated Oct 2), DOWN 14bp from 324bp on Oct 1. The revised FRED sequence reads 302 (Sep 28), 308 (Sep 29), 312 (Sep 30), 324 (Oct 1), 310 (Oct 2) - so the nine-consecutive-widening-sessions narrative carried in prior runs ENDS HERE, and the Oct 1 324 print now looks like a spike rather than a trend extension. CRITICAL READ: this is the first credit observation that contains the plus 29k payroll reaction, and credit TIGHTENED into it. Versus one week ago (308bp on Sep 29) the spread is 2bp wider, so the weekly trend is flat, not up - downgraded from up. Level is still elevated versus the 10-year average near 321bp and the Sep 18 base of 268bp, i.e. 42bp of net widening retained, but the impulse has stopped. DOLLAR - BREAKOUT CONFIRMED: DXY 102.15 (TradingEconomics live, Oct 6), after an Oct 5 close near 102.26 (Dealplexus, Oct 5, day range 101.86-102.54). That takes out the 102.21 52-week high that the index had been pressing for three sessions, and the 52-week range now extends to 102.54. Fourth consecutive advance; plus 3.0 pct on the month, RSI near 74 (overbought). DATA NOTE: Investing.com served 101.87 with a previous close of 101.93 and a 52-week high of 102.21 this run - every one of those matches the PRE-Oct-5 state, so that page is stale and is discarded; TradingEconomics (102.145-102.174, Oct 6) and Dealplexus (102.26, Oct 5) are two independent sources above 102.1 and are carried. Note this reverses last run judgement, which treated the TradingEconomics 102.3 handle as the outlier - it was early, not wrong. Trend up. RATES - LONG END AT A 19-YEAR HIGH AND STILL STEEPENING: 2s10s 0.47 (FRED T10Y2Y, Oct 5), from 0.45 (Oct 2), 0.46 (Oct 1), 0.41 (Sep 30), 0.37 (Sep 29) - ten basis points of steepening in five sessions. Oct 5 closes: 10y 5.315 pct (plus 3.8bp), 2y 4.823 pct (minus 0.2bp), 30y 5.670 pct (plus 4.0bp). Cash closes imply 49bp; FRED constant-maturity 0.47 is carried for series consistency. The decomposition is unchanged and is the whole story: the entire steepening is long-end selloff, the front end has not moved, and the 10y is at its highest since 2007 with the 30y at a two-decade-plus high. Long rates refusing to fall after a plus 29k payroll print is the stagflation tell. Driver on the session was the ISM services release. Fed: roughly 78 pct probability of no change this month; September FOMC minutes due Wednesday. Trend up. BREAKEVENS - FIFTH TEST, STILL ANCHORED: 5y5y forward 2.35 pct (FRED T5YIFR, Oct 2), versus 2.36 (Oct 1) and 2.35 (Sep 28). Brent has round-tripped 30 dollars, credit has widened 42bp net and retraced 14, the dollar has broken to a cycle high and the long end has sold off 11bp on the week - and long-run inflation expectations have moved one basis point. Flat. OIL - THE SECOND DOWN DAY, AND 100 IS THE LINE: Brent 100.33 USD/Bbl (TradingEconomics, Oct 6 live, plus 0.01 pct on the session), versus 101.49 yesterday and roughly 102.25 at the Oct 2 settle - down about 1.9 pct on the week and the clearest two-day decline since the shock began. HDFC Sky (Oct 6) corroborates at 100.7 plus 0.4 pct with WTI 89.7; the two sources bracket the 100.3-100.7 area. SUPPLY IS WINNING: Gulf crude shipments have recovered to 17.5 million barrels a day, about 98 pct of pre-war levels (up from 81 pct in the late-September readings), Saudi Arabia has cut Asian OSPs, and the G7 release of up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel over four months is still feeding through. What has NOT gone away is the seaborne risk premium, which continues to sit in freight, insurance and the Brent-WTI differential rather than in flat price, with Houthi and Hormuz-security attacks ongoing. Trend down for a second run. EQUITY VOL - DIVERGENCE NOW RESOLVED THE OTHER WAY: VIX 15.52 (Oct 5 close, plus 1.37 pct), versus 15.31 (Oct 2) and 16.04 one week earlier on Sep 29, so the weekly trend flips to DOWN. With HY OAS also flat on the week, the three-run equity-vol-versus-credit divergence has closed by credit coming to equities rather than the reverse. Oct 5 closes: S&P 500 7,773.99 (plus 0.66 pct), Nasdaq Composite 27,477.31 (plus 1.05 pct, record), Dow 51,267.90 (plus 0.18 pct), Russell 2000 2,853.27 (plus 0.72 pct). Record equity highs alongside a 19-year-high long bond is the single most uncomfortable pairing on the dashboard. GROWTH PROXY - COPPER/GOLD TURNS UP, BUT FOR THE WRONG REASON: 1.60 (copper 6.60 USD/Lbs plus 0.19 pct, gold 4,115.48 USD/t.oz minus 0.59 pct; 6.60/4115.48*1000 = 1.60), up from 1.57 where it had been pinned for three runs. READ THIS CAREFULLY: the ratio rose because GOLD FELL to a two-month low on dollar strength and surging real yields, not because copper signalled a growth impulse - copper is still minus 2.1 pct on the month on Chinese industrial weakness, supported only by AI datacentre demand, the lowest Chilean output since February 2011 and a strike vote at Antofagasta Centinela. Trend up, signal quality poor. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - THE RELEASE IS TOMORROW: NFCI minus 0.548 for the week ending Sep 25 (FRED NFCI, updated Sep 30), NEXT RELEASE OCT 7. Sequence minus 0.559, minus 0.560, minus 0.558, minus 0.553, minus 0.548 across five weeks - half a basis point of tightening against what was 56bp of HY widening, a MOVE above 100, an 11bp long-end selloff and now a dollar breakout. Loosest of the cycle, carried flat, eighth run of divergence. Tomorrow resolves it, and it now has a credit retracement to explain as well. REAL ECONOMY - ONE NEW PRINT: ISM SERVICES 54.9 for September (ISM via PR Newswire, released Oct 5 10:00 ET), down from 55.4 in August, 27th consecutive month of expansion, prices index 74.0. This was the session driver for yields. Dashboard ism_pmi field remains ISM MANUFACTURING at 54.5 for September (Oct 1 release, from 54.6, prices paid 77.9), trend down - both ISM series are now decelerating from expansionary levels with cost pressure elevated in each. Initial claims 197k for the week ending Sep 26 (FRED ICSA; 198k, 198k, 207k, 207k before it), NEXT RELEASE OCT 8 - still the only indicator that has not confirmed the payroll weakness, and Thursday is the test. Flat. Sahm Rule 0.00 for September (FRED SAHMREALTIME, released Oct 2), from minus 0.07 in August, minus 0.03 in July, plus 0.07 in June, plus 0.10 in May - first non-negative print of the cycle, trigger is plus 0.50, so direction not signal. Next print Nov 6. Trend up. UMich sentiment 48.1 (final September, four-month low, one-year inflation expectations 4.6 pct), next print Oct 9. Building permits 1,403k (August; 1,433k July, 1,374k June, 1,410k May, 1,423k April), next release Oct 20. LEI y/y carried at minus 0.7 pct - August index 99.5, minus 0.1 pct on the month (first monthly decline since March) with a minus 0.1 pct six-month growth rate; the Conference Board release does not publish a y/y figure and the NEXT RELEASE IS OCT 22, later than the mid-October date carried in prior runs. Flat. BOND VOL - UNRESOLVED, AND THE SOURCE CONFLICT IS NOW FOUR-WAY: MOVE carried UNCHANGED at 105.74 for a second run because no verifiable fresh print exists. This run returned four mutually inconsistent quotes: Investing.com 107.29 at minus 0.78 pct dated 02/10, TradingView TVC-MOVE 83.9982 at minus 3.36 pct with no timestamp, Convex 74.67, and NYU V-Lab 88.41 which is a GARCH FORECAST and not the index. IMPORTANT REVISION TO THE LAST RUN CALL: the Investing.com 02/10 stamp is day/month on that site, i.e. OCTOBER 2, not February 10 - the prior run read it as a stale February tick and discarded it on that basis, which was probably a date-format error. 107.29 is therefore plausibly a real Oct 2 close and would be a new high above the 106.61 Oct 1 record. It is NOT carried, because a number that would set a record should not enter the dashboard on one unconfirmable quote while two other venues show the mid-70s to mid-80s. Independently confirmed anchors remain: 101.82 on Sep 29, first close above 100 since the spring, plus 35 pct in September, a weekly surge of 19-29.7 pct that was the largest since April 2025 (Benzinga, Bloomberg, Benefits and Pensions Monitor, KuCoin). Level carried, trend up, source still unwired - this remains the second-worst data gap on the dashboard. CARRIED STANDING ASSUMPTIONS, no free live source found this run: SOFR-OIS 0bp, EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis minus 10bp. Global liquidity 1 (stable). BDTI DATA FLAG - FIFTEENTH consecutive run carried at 4,899 and formally non-informative. Investing.com still frozen at 1,107.00 dated 31/03, MacroMicro 403, Barchart and Baltic Exchange subscription-only. Public commentary puts the real BDTI all-time high near 1,900, so 4,899 is not on a comparable scale and must NOT be read as a level. Wire a paid source or drop the tile. PICTURE: the stagflation squeeze has not ended, it has changed instrument. The two blades that defined the last fortnight - crude above 100 and relentless credit widening - are both retreating: Brent is down a second day as Gulf exports return to 98 pct of pre-war levels, and HY OAS tightened 14bp in the first observation to contain the payroll shock. In their place the pressure has moved to the dollar and the long end, which is a worse place for it to be. DXY has broken a 52-week high, the 10y is at a 2007 high and the 30y at a two-decade high, gold has been knocked to a two-month low, and all of that is happening while the front end does not move and equities print records. A long-end-and-dollar squeeze with anchored breakevens and a flat front end is not an inflation-expectations problem; it is a term-premium and global-dollar-funding problem, and the two tiles that would show funding stress - SOFR-OIS and the cross-currency basis - are both standing assumptions rather than live data. That is now the most consequential gap on the board, ahead of MOVE. WATCH: the NFCI release on Oct 7, which has eight weeks of divergence and a credit retracement to account for; the September FOMC minutes on Oct 7; initial claims on Oct 8, the third week of contradiction with the payroll print; UMich on Oct 9; whether HY OAS confirms the reversal or resumes widening; whether DXY holds above 102.21 or fails back inside the range; whether the 10y holds 5.315; whether Brent breaks 100 decisively or the Hormuz premium rebuilds through freight and the Brent-WTI spread; and wiring live SOFR-OIS, cross-currency basis, MOVE and BDTI sources, which are now four blind or assumed tiles out of nineteen.
